The **BWF World Championships** is a badminton tournament organized by the [Badminton World Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badminton_World_Federation). [1] It's the most prestigious badminton competition, offering the most [ranking points](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BWF_World_Ranking), along with the [Summer Olympics badminton events](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badminton_at_the_Summer_Olympics) introduced in 1992. [2] The winners of the tournament are World Champions of the sport and are awarded a gold medal. [3]

The tournament started in [1977](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1977_IBF_World_Championships) and was held once every three years until [1983](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1983_IBF_World_Championships). However, the International Badminton Federation faced difficulty in hosting the first two events as the [World Badminton Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Badminton_Federation), which later merged with the IBF to form one badminton federation, hosted the same tournament a year after the IBF World Championships with the same goals.

Since [1985](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985_IBF_World_Championships), the tournament became biennial and played once every two years until [2005](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_IBF_World_Championships). Starting [2006](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_IBF_World_Championships), the tournament was changed to an annual event on the BWF calendar, except during Summer Olympic years.

As of 2025, only 22 countries have achieved at least a bronze medal in the tournament: 11 from Asia, eight from Europe, two from North America and one from Oceania. Africa is the only confederation that has not won a medal. Canada is the newest country to win a medal in 2025.

At the age of 18, [Ratchanok Inthanon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ratchanok_Inthanon) became the youngest winner of a singles title at the Championships. The **All England Open Badminton Championships** is the world's oldest [badminton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badminton) tournament, held annually in [England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/England). With the introduction of the [BWF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badminton_World_Federation)'s latest grading system, it was given [Super Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BWF_Super_Series) status in 2007, upgraded to Super Series Premier status in 2011, and designated a Super 1000 event at the birth of the World Tour in 2018. [1] The Super 1000 events, held in four historic strongholds of the sport of badminton (Great Britain, China, Malaysia and Indonesia) are the highest level events below the World Championships and Olympic Games tournaments, and broadly equivalent in stature, though apart from the All-England not in historicity, to the [Grand Slam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Slam_(tennis)) tournaments in tennis. [2]

The world's first [open tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_tournament) was held in the English town of [Guildford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guildford) in 1898, the success of which led to the All England's inaugural edition, which was held at [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London)'s Horticultural Halls in 1899. Although the inaugural edition consisted of just the doubles format, the singles were introduced from the second edition onward. [3] It was eventually considered – especially after the first [Thomas Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Cup) series in 1949 – the unofficial world championship of the sport until 1977, when the [International Badminton Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Badminton_Federation) launched its [official championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Badminton_Championships). [4]

There were two instances when it was halted – from 1915 to 1919, due to [World War I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_I), and from 1940 to 1946, due to [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II). [5]

The **BWF World Tour Finals**, officially **HSBC BWF World Tour Finals**, which succeeds [BWF Super Series Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BWF_Super_Series_Finals), is an annual season finale [badminton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badminton) tournament which is held every December of a year where the players with the most points from that calendar year's events of the [BWF World Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BWF_World_Tour) compete for total prize money of at least [US$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_dollar) 2,500,000.

## Features

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=BWF_World_Tour_Finals&action=edit&section=1)]

### Prize money

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=BWF_World_Tour_Finals&action=edit&section=2)]

The tournament offers total prize money of US$3,000,000. [1] The prize money is distributed via the following formula: [2]

The prize money distribution (as of [2025](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_BWF_World_Tour_Finals) editions) are:

| Round | Men's singles | Women's singles | Men's doubles | Women's doubles | Mixed doubles |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Winner | US$240,000 | US$240,000 | US$252,000 | US$252,000 | US$252,000 |
| Runner-up | US$120,000 | US$120,000 | US$120,000 | US$120,000 | US$120,000 |
| Semi-finalist | US$60,000 | US$60,000 | US$60,000 | US$60,000 | US$60,000 |
| 3rd in Group | US$33,000 | US$33,000 | US$39,000 | US$39,000 | US$39,000 |
| 4th in Group | US$18,000 | US$18,000 | US$21,000 | US$21,000 | US$21,000 |

### World ranking points

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=BWF_World_Tour_Finals&action=edit&section=3)]

Main article: [BWF World Ranking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BWF_World_Ranking)

Below is the point distribution table for each phase of the tournament based on the [BWF points system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BWF_World_Ranking) for the BWF World Tour Finals event. [3]

| Winner(s) | Runner(s)-up | Semi-finalists | 3rd in group | 4th in group |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 14,000 | 12,000 | 10,000 | 8,900 | 7,800 |

### Eligibility

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=BWF_World_Tour_Finals&action=edit&section=4)]

At the end of the BWF World Tour circuit, top eight players/pairs in the BWF World Tour standing of each discipline, with the maximum of two players/pairs from the same member association, are required to play in a final tournament known as the BWF World Tour Finals. [4]

Only the top 14 results from the BWF World Tour tournaments during the year and a maximum of 3 results from Super 100 will count towards the ranking for BWF World Tour Final [5]

If two or more players are tied in ranking, the selection of players will based on the following criteria: [4]

- The players who participated in the most BWF World Tour tournaments;
- The players who collected the most points in BWF World Tour tournaments starting on 1 July that year.

The All England Open Badminton Championships is an annual British badminton tournament created in 1899. For four decades beginning 1954, the Championships was held at the [Wembley Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wembley_Arena), [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London) but since 1994, it has been played at the [Arena Birmingham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arena_Birmingham) in the city of [Birmingham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birmingham), [United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom). [1] The Gentlemen's Singles was first contested in 1900. [2] Below is the **list of the winners at the [All England Open Badminton Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_England_Open_Badminton_Championships)** in gentlemen's singles. The tournament was cancelled between 1915–1919 because of [World War I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_I), and between 1940–1946 because of [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II).

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_All_England_men%27s_singles_champions&action=edit&section=1)]

In the Amateur era, [Rudy Hartono](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rudy_Hartono) (1968–1974, 1976) holds the record for the most titles in the Gentlemen's Singles, winning All England eight times. Hartono also holds the record for most consecutive titles with seven from 1968 to 1974.

Since the Open era of badminton began in late 1979 [3] [4] [*[pageneeded](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citing_sources)*] with the inclusion of professional badminton players from around the world in 1980, [Lin Dan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lin_Dan) (2004, 2006–2007, 2009, 2012, 2016) holds the record for the most Gentlemen's Singles titles with six. [Morten Frost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morten_Frost) (1986–1987), [Hariyanto Arbi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hariyanto_Arbi) (1993–1994), [Poul-Erik Høyer Larsen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poul-Erik_H%C3%B8yer_Larsen) (1995–1996), Lin Dan and [Lee Chong Wei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Chong_Wei) (2010–2011) share the record for most consecutive victories with just two.

This event was won without losing a single game in the entire tournament during the Open era as many as twelve times. The first to accomplish this was [Prakash Padukone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prakash_Padukone) who won in the very first Open era edition in 1980, followed by Morten Frost in 1986 and 1987, [Yang Yang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yang_Yang_(badminton)) in 1989, Poul-Erik Høyer Larsen in 1996, [Sun Jun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sun_Jun_(badminton)) in 1998, [Pullela Gopichand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pullela_Gopichand) in 2001, [Muhammad Hafiz Hashim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muhammad_Hafiz_Hashim) in 2003, [Chen Jin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chen_Jin_(badminton)) in 2008, Lin Dan in 2009 and 2012 and Lee Chong Wei in 2011.

[Liem Swie King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liem_Swie_King) is the only player in history to reach the All England Open Badminton Gentlemen's Singles Final in both Amateur and Open era. He managed to do so seven times, winning on three occasions.

[Badminton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badminton) had its debut as an official event on the [1992 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics) and has been contested in nine Olympiads. 74 different nations have appeared in the Olympic badminton competitions, with 17 appearing all nine times. It is governed by the [Badminton World Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badminton_World_Federation).

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Badminton_at_the_Summer_Olympics&action=edit&section=2)]

The [1972 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_Summer_Olympics) saw the inaugural staging of [badminton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badminton), as a demonstration sport. Two decades later, after a successful exhibition at the [1988 games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988_Summer_Olympics), the sport was officially introduced to the Olympics in 1989, and debuted in competition at the [1992 Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics) where 4 events were held, with singles and doubles events for both men and women. Four medals were awarded in each event, including two bronzes. At the following Games in [1996](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_Summer_Olympics), had 5 events with the addition of mixed doubles. Since 1996 there is a playoff between the two semi-final losers to determine the sole winner of the [bronze medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronze_medal). This format has continued to [2024 Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badminton_at_the_2024_Summer_Olympics).

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

[Lin Dan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lin_Dan) is the first player in mens single to win consecutive golds in the [2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Summer_Olympics) and [2012 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics).

[Gao Ling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gao_Ling) won a total of 4 olympic medals in badminton, with 2 being consecutive mixed doubles gold

[Badminton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badminton) is a sport contested at the [Summer Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summer_Olympic_Games). Badminton was first held as a [demonstration sport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demonstration_sport) at the [1972 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_Summer_Olympics), and was an exhibition sport at the [1988 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988_Summer_Olympics); the men's and women's singles and doubles have been held at every Summer Olympics since the [1992 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics). [1] The mixed doubles badminton tournament started in the [1996 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_Summer_Olympics). [2]

The [Badminton World Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badminton_World_Federation) (BWF) rankings are used to determine the qualification of the players for the tournament. Nations can enter a maximum of two players each in the men's and women's singles if both are ranked in the world's top 16; otherwise, one quota place until the roster of thirty-eight players has been completed. Similar regulations also apply to the players competing in the doubles, as the NOCs (National Olympic Committees) can enter a maximum of two pairs if both are ranked in the top eight, while the remaining NOCs are entitled to one until the quota of 16 highest-ranked pairs is filled. The host nation, if it has not already qualified two competitors, receives at least either two singles players or one pair. [3]

[Gao Ling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gao_Ling) is the all-time leader for the most Olympic medals in badminton, with two golds, one silver, and one bronze; [Fu Haifeng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fu_Haifeng) (two golds, one silver), [Zhang Nan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhang_Nan_(badminton)), [Zhao Yunlei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhao_Yunlei), [Viktor Axelsen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viktor_Axelsen) and [Kim Dong-moon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kim_Dong-moon) (two golds, one bronze) each, [Gil Young-ah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gil_Young-ah) and [Chen Long](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chen_Long) (one each) and [Lee Chong Wei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Chong_Wei) (three silvers) are second for the most medals in badminton, each with three. [Fu Haifeng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fu_Haifeng), [Gao Ling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gao_Ling), [Ge Fei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ge_Fei_(badminton)), [Gu Jun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gu_Jun), [Kim Dong-moon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kim_Dong-moon), [Lee Yang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Yang), [Lin Dan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lin_Dan), [Viktor Axelsen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viktor_Axelsen), [Wang Chi Lin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wang_Chi-Lin), [Zhang Jun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhang_Jun_(badminton)), [Zhang Nan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhang_Nan_(badminton)), [Zhang Ning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhang_Ning) and [Zhao Yunlei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhao_Yunlei) are the all-time leaders for the most gold medal wins, with two. [4] In the 1992 Summer Olympics, future married couple [Susi Susanti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susi_Susanti) and [Alan Budikusuma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Budikusuma) won Indonesia their first ever Olympic gold medals since their first Olympic participation in [1952](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1952_Summer_Olympics), while brothers [Jalani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jalani_Sidek) and [Razif Sidek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Razif_Sidek) were the first Malaysian Olympic medalists since Malaysia first participated in the [1964 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1964_Summer_Olympics). [5] [Mia Audina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mia_Audina) won her first silver in the 1996 Olympics representing Indonesia, but won her second silver in the [2004 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Summer_Olympics) with the Netherlands, the only badminton medalist to ever win for two different countries. [6] In the [2000 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badminton_at_the_2000_Summer_Olympics), China swept the [women's doubles tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badminton_at_the_2000_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_doubles), winning all three medals, making it the only sweep in Olympic badminton history. [7] Indonesia also did this in the [1992 Olympics men's singles tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badminton_at_the_1992_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles), but there was no bronze medal match in that Games so the medal was shared with Danish player [Thomas Stuer-Lauridsen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Stuer-Lauridsen). In the [2012 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badminton_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics), China became the first country to win all five disciplines' gold medal in history, and as of 2024 the only clean sweep in the same Games. Indonesia became the second to achieve this feat, stretching from its first gold in the [1992 women's singles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badminton_at_the_1992_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_singles) to [2020 women's doubles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badminton_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_doubles). [8]

As of the [2024 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badminton_at_the_2024_Summer_Olympics), China has been the most successful nation in badminton, winning 52 medals; 37 of them were from the women's singles and doubles and mixed doubles tournaments. Indonesia, South Korea (both 22 medals), and Malaysia (11) are the only other nations to have more than ten medals. As many as 126 medals (44 gold, 44 silver, and 48 bronze) have been awarded to 168 medalists from 13 NOCs. [9] There were four additional bronze medal winners in the 1992 Summer Olympics because no bronze medal matches were played in any of the four tournaments. [10]

# BWF World Ranking - Wikipedia
URL: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BWF_World_Ranking
Type: text/html

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

Badminton world ranking

The **BWF World Ranking** is the official ranking of the [Badminton World Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badminton_World_Federation) for badminton players who participate in tournaments sanctioned by [Badminton World Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badminton_World_Federation). It is used to determine the qualification for the [World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BWF_World_Championships) and [Summer Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badminton_at_the_Summer_Olympics), [1] as well as [BWF World Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BWF_World_Tour) tournaments. [2] Seedings of draws at all BWF-sanctioned tournaments are conducted using the BWF World Ranking. [3] Players under 19 years of age are eligible to rank in the [BWF World Junior Ranking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BWF_World_Junior_Ranking), which were introduced in January 2011. The following lists are the rankings: [4]

## Overview

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=BWF_World_Ranking&action=edit&section=1)]

The ranking points are awarded based on the level and progress of the tournament from each player/pair. Ranking points calculated are based on the tournaments each players/pairs participate in from the last 52 weeks. If a player or pair has participated in ten or fewer World Ranking tournaments, then the ranking is worked out by adding together the points won at tournaments in the last 52 weeks. If a player or pair has participated in 11 or more World Ranking tournaments, only the 10 highest points scored in the tournaments during the 52-week period count towards their ranking. The highest possible ranking points are 124,000 as of 2022 but will soon increase to 125,000 in 2023 with 4 Super 1000 Tournaments. [1] [5] [6] Though the highest points ever achieved are 123,905 by the korean men’s double pair of Kim Won-ho and Seo Seung-jae on 14 April 2026.[*[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed)*]

The **2019 BWF World Championships** was a [badminton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badminton) tournament which was held from 19 to 25 August 2019 at [St. Jakobshalle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Jakobshalle) in [Basel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basel), Switzerland. [1]

## Host city selection

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2019_BWF_World_Championships&action=edit&section=1)]

Basel was chosen to be the host of the 2019 edition of the championships over [2020 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Summer_Olympics) host city, [Tokyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyo). [2] The bid were approved by the Badminton World Federation during a council meeting in [Kuala Lumpur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuala_Lumpur), [Malaysia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malaysia). [3]

Type: text/html

's doubles pair to do so together and the first consecutive Olympic badminton champions not to represent the People's Republic of China. [4] In the bronze-medal match, defending medalists [Aaron Chia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Chia) and [Soh Wooi Yik](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soh_Wooi_Yik) of [Malaysia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malaysia_at_the_2024_Summer_Olympics) defeated [Denmark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denmark_at_the_2024_Summer_Olympics)'s [Kim Astrup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kim_Astrup) and [Anders Skaarup Rasmussen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anders_Skaarup_Rasmussen), 16–21, 22–20, 21–19. [5] The pair saved four match points during the second game to claim Malaysia's third consecutive medal in the event. [6]

## Format

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Badminton_at_the_2024_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men%27s_doubles&action=edit&section=1)]

Lee Yang *(left)* pictured with Wang Chi-lin *(right)* during the medal ceremony.

The 17 teams were split into three groups of four pairs and one group of five pairs. They played a [round-robin tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Round-robin_tournament) with the top-two ranked teams advancing to the knockout stage. Each match was played in a [best-of-3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Playoff_format#Best-of-three_playoff). [7]
